newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba prepared to give Lima rebels asylum - Fujimori.
newsitem.headline: Cuba prepared to give Lima rebels asylum - Fujimori.

text.p: Cuba would be willing to give asylum to leftist rebels holding hostages in Lima if all parties involved, including the rebels, agreed, Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said after talks with Cuban President Fidel Castro on Monday.

Fujimori, on an unexpected visit to Havana, told a news conference he had raised the issue of possible Cuban asylum for the rebels during talks with Castro on resolving the 76-day-old Lima hostage crisis. Cuba indicated it was willing to take the rebels, he said.
"Cuba is willing to cooperate in the framework for this asylum, but not to participate as a mediator," said Fujimori, who arrived in Havana earlier on Monday after visiting the Domican Republic.
Some 20 Marxist rebels are holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
Fujimori's comments followed weeks of speculation that Cuba might be asked to play a role to end the crisis. Cuba had declined all comment on such speculation.
Communist-ruled Cuba was cited in foreign news reports as a possible mediator or as a place of refuge for the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels.
